stem: Which part of a cell holds the enzymes for respiration, and is where most of the energy is released?
hint: Animal and plant cells both have it. A muscle cell has a lot of them.
working: Respiration releases energy, and most of it is released in the mitochondria.

misconceptions.message: That is the jelly where many reactions happen. Respiration has its own structure.
The nucleus holds the genetic material. It does not release energy.

stem: Which part of a cell holds the genetic material and controls what the cell does?
hint: In most animal cells it is the biggest structure you can see under a light microscope.
working: The genetic material is kept in the nucleus, and it controls the cell's activities.

misconceptions.message: DNA is the molecule. The question asks for the structure that holds it.
The membrane controls what goes in and out, not the cell's activities.

stem: Which part of a plant cell contains chlorophyll, the green pigment that absorbs light for photosynthesis?
hint: Animal cells never have it, and not every plant cell does either.
working: Chlorophyll sits inside the chloroplasts, and that is where photosynthesis happens.

misconceptions.message: Chlorophyll is the green pigment. The question asks for the structure it sits in.
The cell wall gives strength and support. Light is absorbed somewhere else.

hint: Work from the outside in. A plant cell has two layers around it.
answers: cell wall, cell membrane, nucleus, chloroplast
cell wall, cell membrane, nucleus, chloroplasts
working: A is the stiff cell wall, B is the cell membrane just inside it, C is the nucleus and D is a chloroplast. So: cell wall, cell membrane, nucleus, chloroplast.

misconceptions.answer: cell membrane, cell wall, nucleus, chloroplast
misconceptions.message: The two outer layers are swapped. The wall is the stiff outside layer.

stem: Put these in size order, smallest first. Write the letters with commas between them. A a cell, B an atom, C the nucleus of a cell, D a molecule.
hint: Ask what each one is made of. Anything built from smaller things is bigger than them.
working: Atoms join to make molecules, molecules build up the nucleus, and the nucleus sits inside the cell. So B, D, C, A.

misconceptions.message: A cell is bigger than its own nucleus. The nucleus sits inside it.

stem: Root hair cells are plant cells, but they have no chloroplasts. Explain why.
hint: Think about where root hair cells are, and what chloroplasts are for.
working: Root hair cells are underground where there is no light, and chloroplasts are only useful for photosynthesis, which needs light.
mark_scheme: 2 marks. 1 mark: root hair cells are underground, so no light reaches them. 1 mark: chloroplasts are where photosynthesis happens, and photosynthesis needs light, so chloroplasts would be no use there.
